purpose: Re-evaluate the rejected local selector-5 assignment without relying on the DC-excluding spectral estimator that selected probe .12 parameters.
interpretation: The valve did transmit factory counter 1. It used an alternate 433.363 MHz solicitation channel, so the single-center analyzer missed it; its absence was not evidence of paired progression.
The progressively shortening LED phases correspond to a structured multi-channel fallback sweep after stage-0 rejection, not to unmodeled post-assignment challenges.
The spectral estimator used to choose probe .12 excludes bins within 100 kHz of the SDR center. One accepted-stock prelude tone falls in that region, invalidating the earlier DEVIATN 0x46 inference.

Symbol-resolved comparison proves that probe .12 transmitted a much wider prelude than stock and retained the ordinary wake polarity. Stock uses a narrower prelude with polarity reversed at the prelude-to-wake boundary.

Do not change the ordinary assignment payload, carrier, wake, sync instant, or branch selection. First emit a non-pairing bench matrix with prelude-only inversion and bounded offset/deviation candidates, measure each through the SDR, and select the least-error waveform before another physical valve trial.
